description: SURFACED by the fz-s2b investigation (at 6efa9fc16). Observed while constructing cross-file macro repros: 'require M' alone is NOT sufficient to invoke M's macro via a qualified call 'M.tag(...)' — it fails with 'macro/not-required' because lookup_module_path has no global-name fallback; the module name must additionally be bound via 'alias M' or 'import M'. Cross-file SYMBOL identity is global, but namespace VISIBILITY is per-code. QUESTION: is this asymmetry intended — that a macro needs BOTH 'require' (for the requirement guard) AND 'alias'/'import' (for name binding) to be called qualified cross-file? Elixir's 'require M' alone DOES permit 'M.macro()'. Decide the intended semantics and either add the global-name fallback in lookup_module_path so 'require M' + 'M.macro()' works (Elixir parity), or document the intended requirement explicitly as a provable fact. Low priority — narrow surface. Related: fz-s2b.

comments.text: SPIKE 2026-07-09: prototype e199bec6 on branch coord/spike-fz-osx-require-macro supports promotion. Root cause: require records required macro IDs but does not bind the module name into namespace; qualified macro expansion requires lookup_module_path visibility before the macro/not-required guard. Recommended implementation: make require bind the required module's default alias while separately preserving the required macro permission set; add tests for bare require M + M.macro(), missing require still macro/not-required, and dotted require Foo.Bar aliasing Bar if Elixir parity is intended. Prototype passed focused require/macro/frontdoor tests and pre-commit check/clippy.

COORDINATOR VERIFY 2026-07-09: landed on integration as 7ad58b8b9 (fz-osx: bind required module paths). Fold gates rerun from integration HEAD: cargo test --lib passed (1292 passed, 6 ignored); cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings passed; focused cargo test --lib require, cargo test --lib remote_macro, and cargo test --test fz2_cli remote_macro passed. Implementation/audit worktrees were temporary; spike prototype superseded by the landed integration commit.

title: Cross-file macro invocation needs alias/import to bind the module name; bare require M + qualified M.macro() fails macro/not-required
